def: A drug that inhibits CYP17A1 (17-alpha-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase), shutting down androgen synthesis in the adrenals, testes and tumor. Used in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, given with prednisone to offset mineralocorticoid excess.
Presence of red cells with irregular, spiky projections of varying length (acanthocytes). Seen in abetalipoproteinemia, vitamin E deficiency, liver disease and McLeod syndrome.
A ketone body made by the liver from fatty acids when insulin is low. It accumulates in diabetic ketoacidosis and is the ketone detected by urine nitroprusside tests.
The sugar added to the H antigen by the A transferase enzyme to create blood group A. Blood group B instead has galactose added.

A cell or structure that stains pink-red with the acidic dye eosin. Pituitary growth hormone and prolactin cells are acidophils, and shrunken acidophilic bodies mark apoptotic hepatocytes in viral hepatitis.
The Krebs cycle enzyme that converts citrate to isocitrate through an intermediate, cis-aconitate. Inhibited by fluoroacetate, and a cytosolic form also regulates iron metabolism.
A common benign, soft, flesh-colored skin outgrowth on a stalk, usually in skin folds such as the neck and axillae. Associated with obesity and diabetes.
Clubbing of the fingers and toes with swelling of the soft tissue and new bone formation, seen in a small subset of Graves disease patients, along with exophthalmos and pretibial myxedema.
A cap-like vesicle over the head of a sperm containing digestive enzymes (e.g., hyaluronidase, acrosin). Its contents are released in the acrosomal reaction to penetrate the egg's zona pellucida.
A fibrous amphibole type of asbestos, one of the straight needle-like forms linked to mesothelioma and lung cancer.
Describes congenital heart defects without cyanosis, because blood is shunted left to right or flows obstructed. Examples are VSD, ASD, PDA and coarctation.
Adhesion molecules on endothelial cells of lymph nodes and other tissues that bind homing receptors on lymphocytes, directing which tissues they migrate into.
A nucleotide analog antiviral that blocks hepatitis B virus DNA polymerase. Used for chronic hepatitis B and can cause kidney toxicity.
Surgical removal of the adenoids (pharyngeal tonsil tissue at the back of the nasal cavity), often done for obstructive sleep apnea or recurrent ear infections in children.
Fear of drafts of air, a classic symptom of rabies along with hydrophobia. Air blowing on the face triggers painful pharyngeal spasms.
A further fall in core body temperature after rewarming begins in hypothermia, as cold peripheral blood returns to the core. Avoided by rewarming the trunk before the extremities.
A lab test that measures how platelets clump in response to agonists such as ADP, collagen, epinephrine and ristocetin. Absent aggregation points to Glanzmann thrombasthenia.
An antidepressant that acts as a melatonin (MT1/MT2) receptor agonist and serotonin 5-HT2C antagonist. Used for major depression, also with sleep disturbance.
Speech lacking grammatical structure, with short telegraphic phrases missing small function words. A feature of Broca (nonfluent) aphasia.
Recombinant interleukin-2 that stimulates T cell and NK cell growth. Used to treat metastatic renal cell carcinoma and melanoma; can cause capillary leak syndrome.
Formation of antibodies against foreign red cell antigens from another person, such as an Rh-negative mother exposed to Rh-positive fetal cells. Can cause hemolytic disease of the newborn.
The late stage of lung development in which saccules divide into mature alveoli. It is disrupted in bronchopulmonary dysplasia of premature infants.
A toxin of Amanita phalloides mushrooms that binds RNA polymerase II, blocking mRNA synthesis. Causes severe liver failure after a delay of 6 to 24 hours.
The main inhibitory neurotransmitter of the central nervous system, made from glutamate. It opens chloride channels (GABA-A) and is enhanced by benzodiazepines and barbiturates.
A substance fully removed from plasma in one pass through the kidney by filtration and secretion. Its clearance estimates effective renal plasma flow.
Anti-inflammatory drugs (5-aminosalicylic acid, e.g., mesalamine, sulfasalazine) used for mild ulcerative colitis and Crohn disease. Act locally in the gut.
Describes a molecule with both a water-loving (hydrophilic) end and a fat-loving (hydrophobic) end, such as phospholipids and bile salts. Lets them form micelles and membranes.
The rapid, stronger secondary immune response on re-exposure to an antigen, driven by memory B and T cells. Also called a memory response.
A pregnancy in which a gestational sac forms but no embryo develops, also called a blighted ovum. Ultrasound shows an empty sac and it usually ends in miscarriage.
An embryonic precursor cell from mesoderm that gives rise to endothelial cells and early blood vessels. Driven by VEGF during vasculogenesis.
Invasion of blood vessel walls by organisms or tumor, causing thrombosis and tissue infarction. Classic for Aspergillus and Mucor molds.
Complete absence of amniotic fluid, a severe form of oligohydramnios. Often from renal agenesis or ruptured membranes, leading to Potter sequence and pulmonary hypoplasia.
Combined variation in red cell size (anisocytosis) and shape (poikilocytosis) on a blood smear, seen in severe anemias such as thalassemia major.
Relating to the forearm, as in the antebrachial fascia and the medial and lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerves.
A straight, needle-like amphibole form of asbestos, linked to asbestosis, lung cancer and mesothelioma.
Black pigment deposition in the lungs and lymph nodes from inhaled carbon (soot, urban pollution, coal dust). Generally harmless unless it progresses to coal workers' pneumoconiosis.
Conduction of a nerve or cardiac impulse in the direction opposite to normal. An antidromic AV reentrant tachycardia goes down the accessory pathway, producing a wide QRS.
Older name for antibodies against thyroid peroxidase, found in Hashimoto thyroiditis.
Autoantibodies against the mitochondrial pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, the hallmark of primary biliary cholangitis.
A protein that inhibits protease enzymes, such as alpha-1 antitrypsin, which restrains neutrophil elastase in the lungs. Deficiency causes emphysema.
Autoantibodies against thyroglobulin, found in Hashimoto thyroiditis alongside anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies.
An abnormal connection between the aorta and a nearby heart chamber, usually from a perivalvular abscess in infective endocarditis. Causes new heart block or acute heart failure.
A group of neurons in the lower pons that promotes inspiration, prolonging the inspiratory phase. Inhibited by the pneumotaxic center.
An oral phosphodiesterase-4 inhibitor, raising cAMP and lowering inflammatory cytokines. Used for psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and oral ulcers of Behcet disease.
A DNA site missing its purine base, created when a glycosylase removes a damaged base during base excision repair. AP endonuclease then cuts the backbone.
A DNA site missing its pyrimidine base, created when a glycosylase removes a damaged base during base excision repair. AP endonuclease then cuts the backbone.
A polysaccharide of the mycobacterial cell wall that links mycolic acids to peptidoglycan. Its synthesis is blocked by ethambutol.
The pentavalent oxidized form of arsenic (As5+). It mimics phosphate, uncoupling ATP production in glycolysis.
The trivalent form of arsenic (As3+). It binds sulfhydryl groups, inhibiting enzymes such as pyruvate dehydrogenase and lipoic acid.
Kidney scarring from hardening and narrowing of the renal arterioles, usually due to long-standing hypertension. Causes small granular kidneys and chronic kidney disease.
Barrel-shaped fungal spores formed by fragmentation of hyphae. Coccidioides immitis forms them in its mold phase, and inhaling them causes valley fever.
A class of dissociative anesthetics and drugs of abuse that block NMDA receptors, including ketamine and phencyclidine (PCP).
A pair of small laryngeal cartilages that pivot to open and close the vocal cords. Derived from the pharyngeal arches 4 and 6.
Describes minerals that grow as long, thin, flexible fibers, like asbestos. The inhaled fibers cause asbestosis and mesothelioma.
An atypical antipsychotic given sublingually, with antagonism of dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. Used for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
Reduced interest in social interaction and relationships, a negative symptom of schizophrenia.
A monoclonal antibody against PD-L1, a checkpoint inhibitor that restores T cell attack on tumors. Used in lung, bladder and other cancers.
Showers of cholesterol crystals from ruptured aortic plaques that lodge in small arteries, causing blue toes, livedo reticularis and kidney injury, often after catheterization.
A lesion of uterine spiral arteries in preeclampsia, with fibrinoid necrosis and lipid-laden foamy macrophages in the vessel wall.
